newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Ortiz sees 1997 public finance deficit.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Ortiz sees 1997 public finance deficit.

text.p: Mexico's public finances will show a deficit of around 0.5 percent of GDP by the end of 1997, Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said.

The finance ministry was expecting a "quite considerable" surplus in the second quarter, which would decrease in the second half, leading to an end-year deficit of 15 billion pesos, Ortiz said during a presentation of the government's economic programme to the year 2000, known as Pronafide.
The deficit would be equivalent to about 0.5 percent of gross domestic product, he said.

The decrease in the surplus points to a probable strengthening in economic activity in the second semester, he said, adding salaries would start to increase in real terms in the second half of the year.

He said that between January and May this year 367,000 new permanent jobs had been created, setting the government well on its path to reaching its 800,000 target for this year. ((--Daniel Peerez-Whitaker, Monterrey newsroom +528 345 7617))
